Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

#1590. Boga’s limited minutes put focus on Zhegrova before Lazio

Luciano Spalletti outlined different considerations for Jérémie Boga and Edon Zhegrova before Juventus faced Lazio: Boga was fit for around half an hour, while Zhegrova’s performances had earned him a case for more playing time. His remarks, reported by Pazzi di Fanta and echoed in Juventus’ official press-conference account, point to contrasting immediate options rather than a settled hierarchy.

The distinction is grounded in what Spalletti said about their readiness and impact, not in an announced tactical role for either player. Boga remained available, but with his minutes limited; Zhegrova had impressed the coach with qualities and unpredictable play. Juventus’ official account also said the winger could start against Lazio.

For Boga, the clearest point was physical: Spalletti said he had about 30 minutes in his legs. That makes him an option for a defined contribution, rather than a player the coach said was ready to last a full match. It does not mean Boga was unavailable or ruled out of the selection.

Zhegrova’s case was different. Spalletti praised the qualities he had shown and said his performances warranted more playing time. The official Juventus account added that his unpredictable play could surprise opponents, while also reporting that he could start against Lazio.

That contrast suggests Zhegrova offered a possible route to changing the match through his attacking unpredictability, whereas Boga’s immediate involvement was constrained by fitness. It is an interpretation of Spalletti’s comments, not confirmation that the coach assigned them fixed or mutually exclusive positions. The pair’s different recent contributions have also featured in Juventus coverage of Zhegrova’s attacking impact.

Spalletti’s comments on team balance add an important qualification. The official account said the coach was weighing how to fit several attacking players into the side, taking both the opponent and the team’s overall balance into consideration. Praise for Zhegrova did not, by itself, guarantee a starting place.

The coach also rejected a rigid division between starters and substitutes, saying Juventus needed to widen the group of players considered starters. He was still assessing his selection and how the game might develop, with the possibility that starting certain attackers together would leave fewer options to influence the match later.

That broader approach prevents a simple reading in which Boga becomes a permanent bench option and Zhegrova takes over a defined role. Spalletti’s remarks were about the choices available for this fixture: Boga could contribute for roughly half an hour, while Zhegrova’s performances had strengthened his claim to more minutes. Neither statement settles their status over the season.

There is also a difference between being praised and being selected. Spalletti’s assessment gave Zhegrova positive momentum, and Juventus’ account explicitly left open a start against Lazio, but the coach said the final decision still depended on balance and the opposition. Boga, meanwhile, remained available within the fitness limit Spalletti had described.

The immediate comparison is therefore one of management: Boga’s involvement had a stated physical ceiling, while Zhegrova’s was supported by the coach’s view of his performances and unpredictability. That points to different ways they might help Juventus, without establishing a permanent tactical distinction. Boga’s recent place in the side has also been discussed alongside his selection in an attacking role.

Spalletti’s comments leave the practical question to the team selection and the match itself. Juventus’ official account said Zhegrova could start; Boga was available for around 30 minutes. Those were the clearest parameters ahead of Lazio, with no fixed pecking order announced.

#1589. Sky Germany: Krösche heading for Milan but compensation must be discussed – the situation

Sources in Germany are confirming that Markus Krösche should be announced by AC Milan in the coming weeks, ready to start in January.

It is seemingly not a very well-kept secret by this point that Milan are looking to appoint Krösche as their new Head of Football, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Now, Sky Germany confirm that Krösche’s future likely lies in Italy because a move to Milan is becoming increasingly likely. However, no deal has been finalised yet: officials from both clubs still need to hold talks as Krösche is only on leave from Frankfurt.

His contract, which runs until 2028, is currently still valid. The 46-year-old insisted on having a release clause included in his contract. Specifically, this means that any club wanting to hire him before the summer of 2027 will have to pay a fee of approximately €5-7m, or negotiate with Eintracht.

No advanced talks have yet taken place, but Sky do add that Krösche is expected to take on the role of Head of Football with Milan. A start date of January 1, 2027 – coinciding with the start of the winter transfer window – is being discussed.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt have already settled the question of Krösche’s successor. Joti Chatzialexiou is coming from 1. FC Nürnberg and will take over the position of sporting director. So, it seems like just a matter of time.

#1588. Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch suffers fracture as Andoni Iraola explains latest injury blow

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 17:18

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has offered further detail on the heel injury that has ruled Ryan Gravenberch out of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Fenerbahce.

On Tuesday morning, Liverpool released a statement announcing that the Netherlands international would be unavailable for the trip to Istanbul and would remain on Merseyside for treatment.

Gravenberch was an unused substitute during Liverpool's 1-0 Premier League loss to Arsenal on Sunday, which was originally believed to have been a selection decision from Iraola, who started Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni against the Gunners.

However, Gravenberch's demotion from the first XI was down to his new fitness issue, which Iraola confirmed in his pre-game press conference was a fracture of the heel.

The Liverpool boss conceded that Gravenberch has shown no improvement over the last 48 hours, although he did not rule him out of Sunday's Premier League clash with Crystal Palace.

“I don’t know, it’s a day-to-day thing," Iraola said when asked if Gravenberch could make the trip to Selhurst Park. "It’s a fracture of the heel. It’s about the pain.

"He has been with some discomfort. The other day against Arsenal he was warming up and he was not fully confident. He hasn’t improved since then.

“But it’s going to be something that every day we ask him, every day we see how he is. If he can be available for the weekend, lovely, he would be a very good help for us. But I cannot tell you right now."

Gravenberch played the full 90 in both of Liverpool's last two Champions League games against LASK Linz and Fenerbahce, and his absence could open the door for Nyoni to keep his place in the first XI.

The 19-year-old made his full Premier League debut in the loss to Arsenal, completing 59 minutes of the contest, after featuring for over 80 minutes against LASK and Villarreal.

Asked how big an opportunity Wednesday's game could be for Nyoni with Gravenberch out, Iraola added: "He has to continue in the same place he has been since the beginning of pre-season.

"He's playing most of the games, we trust him, he's doing very well. I think we have to encourage him to continue improving, continue learning, but he's in a very good place."

Dominik Szoboszlai is another midfield option for Liverpool after recovering from a hamstring injury, as the Reds aim to make it four wins from four in the 2026-27 Champions League.

Iraola's men are one of just five teams with nine points from their first three games and occupy third place in the Champions League table, only below Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain on goal difference.

#1587. Spalletti identifies Juventus changes after 3-0 Lazio loss

Luciano Spalletti said Juventus were inferior to Lazio after their 3-0 home defeat on Sunday, 18 October, admitting the performance had surprised him. The assessment, reported by Football Italia, came just days after the Bianconeri had beaten Celta Vigo in the Europa League.

Juventus rarely threatened to recover in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard headed Lazio ahead, Gustav Isaksen added a second with an angled finish and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru sealed the result on a late counter-attack. Spalletti said his side had returned from Vigo at 4am on Friday after their 2-1 comeback win, then had time to recover with the performance staff.

He had made six changes, but felt Juventus were slow in both body and thought. His criticism covered the lack of tempo, ideas, running and willingness to work, as well as the team’s weakness in duels and its response when things went wrong. Those concerns followed a previous Juventus defeat that had also prompted scrutiny of the team’s competitive response.

Spalletti was absent from the touchline because of a ban following his altercation with Cagliari’s Fabio Pisacane; assistant Marco Domenichini deputised. Juventus have 11 points after seven league rounds, eight behind the leaders. Football Italia noted that Igor Tudor’s team had one more point at the same stage last season, while Thiago Motta’s side had collected 13.

Supporters who stayed until the final whistle jeered and insulted the squad. Spalletti said the response now had to come on the pitch, rather than the players giving in to events, and identified two areas for review: how he communicates with the team and the working method. He said he needed to examine his relationship with the players and decide what must change.

Speaking to DAZN Italia after the match, Spalletti said Juventus had neither controlled the game nor shown a clear idea of how to shape it. He considered the performance unacceptable and said he would reflect carefully on it. His next task is to determine whether the adjustment lies in his approach to the group, the work itself, or both.

Federica Mancuso has followed Juventus through every high and low she can remember, growing up in Turin where the club was never just a team but a way of life. Her writing focuses on what actually happens on the pitch, breaking down formations, pressing structures, and the tactical decisions that often go unnoticed in match coverage. She believes understanding how Juventus play is just as important as knowing the scoreline.

#1586. Crystal Palace vs Hoffenheim - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 03 Nov 2026 17:30, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 17:57

In need of a morale-boosting victory, out-of-sorts Crystal Palace welcome Hoffenheim to Selhurst Park for their latest League Phase fixture in the Europa League on Thursday night.

The Eagles sit 15th in the 36-team standings, while their German counterparts are eight places further back in 23rd spot after the first three rounds of fixtures.

After nine Premier League games, Crystal Palace find themselves languishing in the relegation zone having posted two wins, one draw and a joint division-high six defeats, leaving head coach Pierre Sage under increased pressure.

The Eagles, who have also conceded the most goals in the league (21), suffered their third straight top-flight loss last weekend as they were beaten 2-0 by Tottenham Hotspur, a result impacted by the 13th-minute dismissal of striker Jean-Philippe Mateta.

“A problem with performance” is what Sage clearly needs to address, and the Frenchman – appointed in June to succeed Conference League winner Oliver Glasner – now has two important home games against Hoffenheim and Liverpool to potentially save his job in South London.

Palace’s form in their maiden Europa League campaign has been mixed thus far; they thrashed Lech Poznan 4-0 at home on matchday one before losing 3-2 against Lyon and drawing 2-2 with Besiktas, away displays marked by sluggish starts and spirited yet flawed comeback attempts.

The Eagles will take some comfort from having won three of their last five home matches in all competitions (L2), while they also head into Thursday’s contest unbeaten in seven European games at Selhurst Park (W5 D2).

Competing in major European competition for just the fifth time in their history this season, Hoffenheim have accumulated only three points from a possible nine available at the start of their Europa League campaign (W1 L2).

Die Kraichgauer lost their opening two matches against OFI Crete (2-0) and Besiktas (3-2), but they achieved what Palace could not against Lyon, as they secured a convincing 3-0 victory over the French side a fortnight ago to open their account in the League Phase.

This statement win was part of a three-game winning streak for Christian Ilzer’s side across all competitions, but they have since been brought back down to earth by a DFB-Pokal second-round exit on penalties to Holstein Kiel and a 2-0 Bundesliga defeat against Werder Bremen, losing to the latter last Saturday.

Although five defeats in eight Bundesliga games has seen Hoffenheim slip down to 12th place in the table, already six points adrift of the top four, Ilzer has insisted that he is “not worried” about his team and has taken plenty of positives from their spirited performances.

Returning to winning ways on Thursday is not a given, though, as Hoffenheim have prevailed in only one of their last six European away games (D2 L3) while they have lost all five of their previous meetings with English opposition (once to Spurs, twice to Liverpool and Manchester City).

Crystal Palace trio Ismaila Sarr (groin), Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) and Chadi Riad (knee) all remain sidelined with injuries, but Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle) and Quinten Timber (hamstring) may be fit to return to the matchday squad.

Despite his Premier League red card, Mateta is available for selection on Thursday and will likely lead the line for the Eagles, with Yeremy Pino, Dwight McNeil, Eddie Nketiah, Dario Osorio and Evann Guessand all battling for starts in the final third.

Cheick Doucoure and Will Hughes are contenders to start in midfield, while Anan Khalaili and Ben Chilwell could both return as wing-backs at the expense of Oscar Mingueza and Tyrick Mitchell.

As for Hoffenheim, their packed treatment room includes ex-West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal, (thigh), Bambase Conte (adductor), Patrick Wimmer (hamstring), Valentin Gendrey (broken leg), Albain Hajdari (foot), Nathan De Cat (knee) and Max Moerstedt (head).

After missing the defeat at Werder Bremen through suspension, Alexander Prass is available to return and could feature as a central midfielder alongside either Leon Avdullahu or Wouter Burger.

Andrej Kramaric contributed to all three goals in the win against Lyon (one goal, two assists) and the 35-year-old will likely be joined in attack by Adam Daghim, Tim Lemperle and top scorer Adam Hlozek (four goals).

Henderson; Canvot, Disasi, Richards; Khalaili, Wharton, Doucoure, Chilwell; Pino, Nketiah; Mateta

Baumann; Abraha, Kabak, Machida, Rots; Prass, Avdullahu; Kramaric, Daghim; Lemperle, Hlozek

Ten of Hoffenheim’s 13 competitive games this season have produced over 2.5 goals, while each of Crystal Palace’s three Europa League matches this term has seen at least four goals scored, so an entertaining contest could be in store on Thursday.

Both teams are desperate for a victory to boost their knockout qualification hopes, but we can envisage the spoils being shared on this occasion.

#1584. Lazio’s Turin win leaves Juventus eight points off Serie A lead

Juventus lost 3-0 at home to Lazio on Sunday, October 18, as goals from Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru kept the visitors level with Inter at the top of Serie A. The result, reported by Football Italia and confirmed in Juventus’ match report, was Lazio’s first league victory in Turin since October 2017.

Lazio took the lead in the 37th minute after a short corner, with Mattia Zaccagni’s delivery finding Provstgaard for a glancing header from close range. Isaksen made it 2-0 in the 66th, controlling Nuno Tavares’ cross-field pass before cutting inside and finding the far bottom corner.

Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, carrying the ball forward from inside his own half before beating Guglielmo Vicario with an angled drive. Juventus had chances to respond: Randal Kolo Muani had an effort ruled out for offside, while Nick Woltemade and Nico Gonzalez both went close. The match statistics showed 58 per cent possession for the hosts and nine shots apiece, but Lazio registered three efforts on target to Juventus’ two.

The loss came after a demanding week. Juventus had beaten Celta Vigo 2-1 away in the Europa League on Thursday, but had managed only one win in their previous four league rounds. Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Jeff Ekhator and Kamil Grabara were unavailable, while Jeremie Boga returned to the bench. Luciano Spalletti served a touchline ban following his altercation with Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane, leaving assistant Marco Domenichini in charge from the bench.

Lazio needed the win to remain joint leaders, and the result left the Bianconeri with more ground to make up. According to Corriere della Sera, Juventus sit eighth on 11 points, eight behind Inter and Lazio, who have 19 each. The defeat adds to the concern around a season in which Juventus have struggled to turn performances into league results, following their draw with Cagliari.

Corriere also reports Juventus have a goal difference of +1, compared with +12 for Inter and +10 for Lazio. The standings sharpen the pressure on Juventus to respond in the next league rounds, while Lazio leave Turin with a sizeable result and their place alongside Inter at the summit intact.

His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

#1582. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#1580. Moggi points to Juventus leadership after 3-0 Lazio loss

Former Juventus general manager Luciano Moggi said the Bianconeri lacked a coach and failed to perform in their 3-0 home defeat to Lazio, sharpening the focus on the team’s leadership.

In comments reported by Football Italia and Gazeta Express, Moggi argued that Juventus had not simply played badly: in his view, they had not taken to the field at all. He pointed to Gleison Bremer’s public remarks as a reflection of the team’s situation and also criticised the defender’s part in Lazio’s third goal.

Moggi’s assessment followed a bruising night at the Allianz Stadium. Oliver Provstgaard, Gustav Isaksen and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru scored as Lazio won 3-0, with Juventus jeered off by their supporters. Football Italia reported that the result left Juventus eight points behind Inter and Lazio.

Juventus’ defeat to Lazio also unfolded with Luciano Spalletti watching from the stands while serving a ban. After the match, captain Bremer criticised his teammates; Spalletti responded that Bremer shared responsibility for the loss.

Moggi, who previously served as Juventus general manager, framed the performance as a problem of coaching authority rather than a poor display on the pitch. He said the team’s situation could be understood through Bremer’s comments, while directing questions about responsibility beyond the players to those in charge.

Spalletti said after the defeat that he was no longer sure the squad were following him. Moggi challenged that uncertainty, arguing that the team’s circumstances could not be excused by injuries. His criticism landed amid an already public exchange between the coach and his captain over individual responsibility for the defeat.

Asked whether Spalletti should be at risk, with some supporters calling for Antonio Conte, Moggi declined to assess the coach’s position from outside the club and directed the question back to the fans. The exchange leaves the focus on the squad’s response and the relationship between players and coach after a damaging home result.

Spalletti’s comments and the dispute over Bremer’s remarks have kept attention on the dressing-room mood, while Moggi’s intervention has added a former club executive’s criticism to the reaction. Juventus now face the task of addressing the concerns raised in the aftermath of the Lazio defeat, with the next performances set to shape the conversation around the team’s direction. The response from Spalletti after the loss has already become part of that debate.

Federica Mancuso has followed Juventus through every high and low she can remember, growing up in Turin where the club was never just a team but a way of life. Her writing focuses on what actually happens on the pitch, breaking down formations, pressing structures, and the tactical decisions that often go unnoticed in match coverage. She believes understanding how Juventus play is just as important as knowing the scoreline.

#1577. Revealed: Scottish journalist did not include Kylian Mbappe in his Ballon d'Or voting - separately, investigation launched into suspicious bets that returned £149,000 and predicted Harry Kane's glory

Published: 08:24 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EDT, 31 October 2026

Kylian Mbappe was a shock top-10 omission from Scotland's Ballon d'Or vote as scrutiny continues to surround Harry Kane's victory, including the launch of an investigation into suspicious bets.

Kane and Mbappe were locked in a fierce race to be crowned the best player in the world and it was England captain Kane who just edged it at Monday's glitzy ceremony in London.

A full breakdown of how each nation's journalist voted has since come to light and it can be revealed that Scotland's voter did not put Real Madrid and France star Mbappe in his top 10.

The Scottish journalist, who was one of three reporters to leave Mbappe off his top 10, joined by colleagues in Greece and Ukraine, had Kane as his winner, followed by Lamine Yamal and Rodri, both of whom won the World Cup.

Fellow Spaniard Fabian Ruiz ranked fourth, with Erling Haaland, Dayot Upamecano, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Marc Cucurella, Ferran Torres and Lionel Messi completing his top 10.

Only two countries left Kane off the top 10 - Mexico and Ivory Coast - while four nations overlooked Yamal - Belarus, Cameroon, Croatia and Greece. Amazingly, the Greek journalist left out Mbappe AND Yamal, including William Pacho (3rd), Joao Neves (5th), Michael Olise (6th), Gabriel (8th), Marquinhos (9th) and Declan Rice (10th) instead.

Suspicious bets made around the Ballon d'Or has triggered an investigation from French police

Former winner Rodri got 10 first place votes - Croatia, Czech Republic, Guatemala, Iceland, Nigeria, Serbia, the United States, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam - while six countries put Messi on top.

The bigger issue with the voting - as an overall event there were ample problems, as explained by Daily Mail Sport, who was in attendance on the night - was what has been described as suspicious betting.

An investigation by French publication 'Upside', as detailed by the Guardian, has explained that bets that triggered £149,000 in winnings has triggered an inquest by organisers France Football.

Police have been alerted and are looking in to allegations that 12 bets placed on Polymarket - an American cryptocurrency-based platform - were done so with, in the view of organisers, an alarming level of accuracy.

The identified accounts correctly predicted and bet on the eventual top five, leading to internal concerns at France Football that the result had been leaked or compromised.

Upside's findings, which are understood to have since been passed on to police, discovered 12 accounts created in the month of October that made a series of very similar bets. Seven of the accounts only placed bets on the Ballon d'Or market.

France Football go to great lengths to limit the number of people with knowledge of the results prior to announcements on the night. They made sure players and their entourages, including those of Yamal, Mbappe and Kane, were kept in the dark.

But, Upside's investigation has served up some alarming allegations that will now be further examined by French police.

#1576. Juventus host Rennes, beaten on all four European trips to Italy, as Lepaul faces absence

Juventus return to Europa League action against a Rennes side that have lost every European away match they have played in Italy. A third win would strengthen their hold on first place after the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio left them eighth in Serie A.

Juventus need a response, and Europe offers the quickest route to one. Luciano Spalletti’s side host Franck Haise’s Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Matchday 3. They do so as leaders of the league phase. Rennes have four points.

The backdrop is uncomfortable. This is the first match since the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio that left Juventus eighth in Serie A. Spalletti watched that game from the stands while serving a one-match ban. The ban followed a confrontation with Cagliari coach Fabio Pisacane. Assistant Marco Domenichini took charge on the bench.

Afterwards, Spalletti said he needed to take a hard look at his relationship with the players. He also admitted Juventus had been worse than Lazio. The schedule had been tight. The squad got back from Vigo at 4:30am, and it was decided they would not train that day.

The Europa League tells a different story. Juventus opened with a 5-0 home win over N.E.C. Nijmegen on 17 September. A 2-1 win at Celta followed. After that game, the coach spoke of a desire in his side not to settle.

Goals have come freely. Juventus have seven so far. The 2003/04 season is the last time the club hit the eight-goal mark across an opening trio of matches in a major European tournament. Back then, it came in the Champions League.

Randal Kolo Muani is central to that output. He has had a hand in five goals across his last five appearances in the Champions League and Europa League.

A third European win would ease some of the pressure on Spalletti. It would also tighten Juventus’ grip on top spot. The visitors will not make it easy, though. Rennes have lost only once this season.

History favours the hosts. Rennes have lost all four of their European away matches in Italy, each against a different club. Juventus were one of them. In the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup final, Juventus won 4-2 on aggregate. Filippo Inzaghi scored both goals in the 2-0 win in Turin. Zinedine Zidane and Alessandro Del Piero were involved in the build-up to the second. The return leg in France ended 2-2.

Rennes’ campaign began with a goalless draw away at Sturm Graz on 16 September. They then beat OFI Crete at home on 15 October.

⮕ https://t.co/B3s5MTvdVk pic.twitter.com/nObmKpMp3Y

— Stade Rennais F.C. (@staderennais) October 19, 2026

Their preparation has been hit hard. Lepaul hurt his ankle in Sunday’s Ligue 1 defeat at Paris FC and is due to have tests, Get French Football News reported. He asked to come off in added time with the score at 3-3. Haise could not see the striker being fit by Thursday. That would leave Rennes without a key attacking option for their trip to Turin.

For Juventus, the opportunity is clear. A win would build momentum in a league phase that finishes on Thursday 28 January 2027. Rennes return to Europa League action at home to Olympiacos on 5 November 2026.

#1575. Sparta Prague vs Bournemouth - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 03 Nov 2026 17:45, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 18:04

High-flying Bournemouth will endeavour to preserve their 100% Europa League record when they travel to Czechia to face Sparta Prague at epet ARENA on Thursday evening.

While the Cherries occupy third position in the 36-team League Phase standings, the Maroons are down in 16th spot after three matches.

After registering only two wins in their opening eight matches in all competitions (D3 L3), new head coach Marco Rose could not have asked for a stronger response from his Bournemouth side who have put together an exceptional six-game winning streak, scoring 16 goals without reply.

Three consecutive 3-0 victories in three different competitions over AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa during a memorable six-day period were followed by a 2-0 home success over Leeds United in the Premier League last weekend.

Sitting eighth in the Premier League table, Bournemouth have won three top-flight games in a row without conceding for the first time in their history. In addition, the Cherries have won their opening three fixtures of their debut Europa League campaign – becoming the first club to achieve this feat since Sunderland in 1973-74.

Prior to their eye-catching home triumph over Milan, Bournemouth held on for a 2-1 victory away against Real Sociedad on matchday one before securing a comfortable 3-0 home win against Sturm Graz; they are one of only five teams out of 36 who currently boast a perfect record in this season’s competition.

Not since January/February 2014 as a Championship side under former boss Eddie Howe have Bournemouth won seven straight matches in all competitions, while they also head to Czechia bidding to win back-to-back competitive away games for the first time this season.

Competing in European competition for the fourth successive season, Sparta Prague have made a mixed start to their Europa League campaign, posting one win, one draw and one defeat from their opening three matches.

After beating Arara-Armenia 4-1 on the road and drawing 1-1 at home to Lillestrom, the Maroons suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat at Olympiacos a fortnight ago, but head coach Brian Priske will not be too concerned about his team’s chances of knockout qualification just yet.

Scoring goals on a consistent basis is something Priske must address, though, as Sparta have failed to make the net ripple in four of their last five games in all tournaments, and they enter Thursday’s contest following two disappointing domestic results.

The Maroons suffered a fourth-round exit in the Czech Cup following a 2-0 home defeat to Banik last week, while they have fallen eight points behind city rivals Slavia Prague at the Czech First League summit after being held to a goalless stalemate by bottom-half side Bohemians 1905 last Sunday.

Sparta will hope that a European fixture in front of their passionate home fans will spark an upturn in form, as they welcome Bournemouth to epet ARENA having lost only one of their last nine UEFA home matches (W6 D2).

Sparta Prague are still having to cope without Matej Rynes, Adam Karabec (both ankle), Magnus Kofod Andersen (knee) and Emmanuel Uchenna (thigh) due to injury.

John Mercado has scored a team-high seven goals this term, but the winger missed the last two matches with a calf issue and will be assessed ahead of kickoff on Thursday.

Former Wolves defender Ki-Jana Hoever is expected to continue at right-back, joining captain Jaroslav Zeleny, Tobias Guddal and either Viktor Vitalyos or Martin Suchomel in a four-man defence, while Scottish midfielder Andy Irving - signed from West Ham in the summer - will be pushing to earn a recall.

As for Bournemouth, key midfielder Alex Scott (hamstring) is edging closer to a return but will not be ready to feature on Thursday, while Alex Toth and Julian Araujo (both thigh) remain sidelined.

Bafode Diakite is just one game away from a Europa League suspension, but the defender is still in contention to start and could replace James Hill in the first XI, playing alongside Antonio Silva at centre-back.

Ben Gannon-Doak, Lewis Cook, Amine Adli and Eli Junior Kroupi are all pushing to start, while Evanilson will hope to retain his place up front having scored five goals in his last six games in all competitions.

Surovcik; Hoever, Zeleny, Guddal, Vitalyos; Irving, Mannsverk, Sochurek; Jurasek, Vojta, Alcocer

Di Gregorio; Smith, Diakite, Silva, Soler; Adams, Cook; Tavernier, Kroupi, Gannon-Doak; Rodriguez

Bournemouth’s rapid improvements at both ends of the pitch have transformed them into a formidable force, making them firm favourites to come out on top against a goal-shy Sparta Prague outfit.

While the Cherries should not underestimate the Maroons on their own turf, Rose will likely field a strong enough team that can extend their impressive winning streak with another clean sheet to boot.

#1573. Man United boss Michael Carrick appears to ignore Lisandro Martinez after defender sent off for deliberately elbowing Wesley Fofana

Published: 10:04 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 10:21 EDT, 31 October 2026

Michael Carrick could not even look at Lisandro Martinez after the Manchester United defender's moment of madness saw him sent off away at Chelsea.

Martinez, not looking at the ball as a corner was whipped in, went in with his elbow on Wesley Fofana's throat, only a minute or so after picking up a yellow card for pulling back Morgan Rogers.

A VAR review was recommended and Martinez, who was in the headlines earlier this month for calling out the United hierarchy for letting Carrick and the players down, was shown a second yellow card and given his marching orders.

It was a ridiculous decision by Martinez to make the challenge he did on Fofana and Carrick elected not to even acknowledge his centre back as he trudged down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer scored the resulting penalty, given away by Martinez, to make it 2-0.

Lisandro Martinez (left) got ignored by boss Michael Carrick (right) after his sending off

Martinez made a ridiculous decision to lead with his elbow, fouling Wesley Fofana in the box

Director of football Jason Wilcox, explicitly called out by Martinez after a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League to Atletico Madrid, watched on alongside CEO Omar Berrada as Martinez's dire decision making took the game away from Carrick's side, who had been the better team in the first half.

'You can't keep changing, changing, changing the manager,' Martínez said in his Madrid rant. 'What about other areas? [looks up] I can't say more.

'It is easy to say the coach, easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas [points up].

'He [Carrick] does his best. Every season is different. You can't stay with what you did last season.

'The teams knows how you play, they know every detail, if you don't change next season is a big problem.

'Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.

'It is annoying, disappointing coming here and I am not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here.'

But he cost his team dearly away at Chelsea, not just with his defending for the opening goal by Rogers, where Martinez and centre back partner Harry Maguire looked incredibly slow, but also for the reckless foul on Fofana that saw Chelsea awarded a result-sealing penalty.

Martinez had a lot to say in Madrid but he was the key person to blame at Stamford Bridge

Martinez was fined for his comments made in Madrid and he sat down for a pow-wow with the hierarchy to thrash out any differences and to get back on the same page.

Yet, at a time when results on the pitch needed to see huge improvement, not least after the Stretford End booed the players off after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth last weekend, Martinez let his team-mates down on a day where they looked the better side for 45 minutes.

The expectation is that Martinez will leave at the end of the season and it could even be as early as January with no guarantee that United trigger the additional year option they hold on a contract that expires at the end of the season.

#1572. Conceicao starts rehab as month-long layoff remains unconfirmed

Juventus have confirmed Francisco Conceicao suffered a shoulder problem against Lazio, while local reports suggest the winger could miss around a month.

The club’s diagnosis, reported by Portuguese outlet Observador from a Juventus medical update, followed examinations after the injury on Sunday, October 18. Juventus said Conceicao had started rehabilitation, but did not give a return date.

ANSA had reported on Monday, October 19, that Conceicao was due to undergo specific tests at J Medical, with a month on the sidelines a possibility if those checks confirmed a dislocation. Observador’s account of the club update subsequently described the injury as a possible glenohumeral dislocation pending the J Medical examinations.

The distinction matters for the timetable: the roughly one-month estimate comes from local media reporting, not a recovery date announced by Juventus. Observador also reported that the club had not disclosed the expected length of his absence.

Conceicao’s injury came during the 3-0 defeat to Lazio, leaving Juventus to assess their options on the wing while he begins rehabilitation. A month-long layoff would keep the Portugal international out of selection for a significant run of fixtures, although the club has not confirmed that timeframe.

The setback puts fresh focus on the attacking contribution Juventus lose when Conceicao is unavailable. His goals and assists have been part of his contribution in Turin, and the injury adds a selection concern after a difficult result against Lazio. He has also attracted attention around his involvement at the club, as Conceicao’s role at Juventus has been discussed in recent coverage.

For now, Conceicao’s rehabilitation is under way. Juventus have yet to publish a target date for his return, while the month-long estimate remains the timeframe reported by local media.

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1571. Sunderland vs Dinamo Zagreb - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 03 Nov 2026 18:00, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 18:18

Putting their Premier League survival fight to one side, Sunderland return to Europa League action on Thursday night when they welcome Dinamo Zagreb to the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats currently sit ninth in the 36-team League Phase standings, while the Blues are nine places further back in 18th spot after three matches.

Almost six months on from securing a seventh-placed Premier League finish and ending their 53-year wait for European qualification, Sunderland now find themselves rock bottom of England’s top division following a winless seven-game run (D2 L5).

A disappointing 3-1 away defeat to newly-promoted Coventry City last weekend leaves the Black Cats on five points – their lowest tally after nine games in a top-flight campaign since 2016-17 (two) when they were relegated to the second tier.

Despite their poor form, Regis Le Bris’s position as Sunderland head coach is reportedly safe. The Frenchman is said to retain the full support and confidence of the club’s hierarchy, who believe the 50-year-old will turn their fortunes around sooner rather than later.

Away from the Premier League, Sunderland secured a morale-boosting 3-2 home win over Brentford in the EFL Cup fourth round last week, while they remain unbeaten in the Europa League this term, collecting seven points from their opening three games (W2 D1).

Back-to-back victories over AZ Alkmaar (1-0) and Torreense (2-1) were followed by a 1-1 draw with Lech Poznan in Poland a fortnight ago. Returning to winning ways on Thursday would go a long way toward cementing a top-eight spot and automatic qualification for the round of 16.

In stark contrast to Sunderland, Dinamo Zagreb are involved in yet another title battle this season as they endeavour to win a record-extending 27th Croatian top-flight trophy, though two defeats in their last four games have halted their progress.

A surprise 1-0 defeat to Rudes last weekend resulted in the mutual termination of Mario Kovacevic’s contract as head coach, with reserve team boss Jerko Leko having stepped up to take caretaker charge for the next two games while the club search for a successor.

While Dinamo sit four points behind leaders Hajduk Split with a game in hand, the Blues have made a mixed start to their Europa League campaign, posting one win, one draw and one defeat from their opening three matches.

Four points were picked up following a goalless stalemate with Hapoel Be’er Sheva and a 1-0 win over Anderlecht, but they were beaten 4-2 at home to NEC Nijmegen on matchday three, leaving them three points behind Thursday’s opponents Sunderland in the League Phase table.

Dinamo travel to the Stadium of Light having won only one of their last eight European away games (D4 L3), while they have won three and lost three of their previous six encounters with English opposition.

Sunderland’s Daniel Ballard (hamstring), Romaine Mundle (knee) and Habib Diarra (muscle) all remain out with injuries, while Chemsdine Talbi, Jocelin Ta Bi, Melker Ellborg, Alan Browne and Aji Alese are all ineligible for the Europa League.

Nordi Mukiele missed the defeat a Coventry due to concussion protocols and will need to be assessed before kickoff on Thursday, while teenager Juan Angulo (knock) is also a doubt.

Brian Brobbey signed a new long-term contract with the Black Cats on Tuesday, but he may be replaced up front by either Wilson Isidor or Timur Tutierov – who scored in the draw with Poznan – while Kevin Danso, Dayann Methalie, Thomas Meunier and Malick Fofana are all pushing for recalls.

As for Dinamo Zagreb, defender Scott McKenna has been left out of the Scotland squad ahead of November’s international break due to a back strain and will presumably miss Thursday’s match.

The Blues seem to be at full strength elsewhere, though, with Niko Galesic or Stjepan Radeljic set to partner Sergi Dominguez at centre-back in the absence of McKenna.

Star striker Dion Drena Beljo has scored 17 goals in 18 appearances across all competitions this season, at least 13 goals more than any of his teammates. Three of those goals have been netted in two Europa League matches and he is expected to lead the line once again this week.

Roefs; Hume, Danso, O’Nien, Methalie; Xhaka, Sadiki; Meunier, Le Fee, Fofana; Isidor

Kotarski; Galesic, Dominguez, Radeljic, Vinlof; Misic, Ivanusec, Stojkovic; Almena, Beljo, Hoxha

Both teams enter this fixture in desperate need of a positive result to ignite their respective campaigns, and while Dinamo Zagreb will be hoping for an immediate bounce under their caretaker boss, they arrive at the Stadium of Light as clear underdogs.

Taking into account that only Bayer Leverkusen (72) have attempted more shots than Sunderland's 67 in the opening three Europa League matches, the Black Cats' superior firepower could see them navigate their way to a vital victory on home soil.

#1570. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.
