Curbishley is rare among those on this list in that his time in charge ended better than it started.

He was able to recover from humbling defeats to Charlton and Reading to help West Ham pick up more points in the final nine games of the 2006-07 season than they picked up in the first 29.

His one full season was pretty handy too, bringing the luxury of mid-table obscurity and the high point of a goalscoring debut for Freddie Sears.

For a team which has spent much of the last 35 years flitting between excitement and despair, nothingness was underrated.

Yes, he led West Ham to an FA Cup final and a top-half finish, but he also set the team on course for relegation in the following season before being sacked after a 4-0 defeat to a Bolton team that didn’t win another game by more than two all season.

He also came close to botching not one but two promotion campaigns, ultimately sneaking a 1-0 win against Preston after leaving it late to even make the 2004-05 play-offs, relying on his former club Reading losing each of their last three games.

There’s an argument that he would have kept things going in the 2006-07 campaign if he had a fit and firing Dean Ashton at his disposal.

However, based on Pardew’s record at *checks notes* every other club he’s managed since, that seems unlikely.

Allardyce will never be too many West Ham fans’ favourite, but he was brought in to return West Ham to the Premier League and keep them there, and he succeeded.

He even kept the team out of trouble for two of his three seasons in the top flight, though the collapse in the second half of the 2014-15 season was about as bleak as they come.

West Ham were fourth at Christmas but won just three more times before the end of the season, against teams that finished 16th, 18th and 19th in the league.

Pretty uninspiring, for sure, but it would be remiss of us to ignore the fact that he did still take the team into the top four, via wins over Liverpool and Manchester City.

Bilic was the man who gave West Ham fans one of the most enjoyable seasons in living memory, and that’s enough to more than make up for some of the misery the Croatian’s second and third campaigns.

West Ham were simply a joy to watch in the 2015-16 campaign, with Dimitri Payet – given his debut by Bilic – the main orchestrator.

Sure, things tailed off the following season with a limp start to life at the London Stadium, and the wheels threatened to fall off completely before he was replaced by Moyes.

That one season, though, is more than many will achieve in charge of West Ham United – in terms of achievement and the hope Bilic was able to create amongst a pessimistic fanbase.

Look, we don’t like this any more than you, but it’s hard to put Knappsy anywhere other than near the top.

He took over a West Ham team that had been back in the Premier League for just one season and dragged it gradually up the table over the course of several years.

The highlight came in the 1998-99 season with a fifth-place finish, while Redknapp also brought Paolo Di Canio to the club and gave debuts to Joe Cole, Michael Carrick, Rio Ferdinand and Jermain Defoe.

Sure, his tenure didn’t end on the best of terms, but such a thing has been hard to find with any West Ham boss in the Premier League era.

Moyes was brought in to keep West Ham United in the Premier League in November 2017, and he did that.

Moyes was brought in to keep West Ham United in the Premier League in December 2019, and he did that.

Was he brought in to give West Ham two top-seven finishes, three seasons in Europe and lifting the club’s first piece of major silverware in 43 years?

Definitely not. But seeing the Moyesiah rediscover his mojo and create a team that mirrored his successful Everton sides was heart-warming even for neutrals.

That’s as good as the club have had it in god knows how long. No Hammer will ever forget that night in Prague, the like of which now feels very distant.

#1511. Kevin Nisbet's lack of cool proved so costly for Aberdeen at Hampden... and underlines why he's not a man for the big occasion

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 18:27 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EDT, 31 October 2026

In the build-up to this Premier Sports Cup semi-final, Aberdeen captain Kevin Nisbet spoke about the players needing to step up and deliver.

On a woeful run of form as they arrived at Hampden, and with huge pressure mounting on Stephen Robinson, Nisbet insisted the players owed the manager a performance and a result.

Just to take the heat off as much as anything else. With 76 minutes on the clock in this tense and cagey affair with Rangers, Nisbet had a golden opportunity.

With the score locked at 0-0, Stuart Armstrong fed a pass into Nisbet’s path and the ball was crying out to be struck first time.

Nisbet could probably see the whites of Ivor Pandur’s eyes. In the context of the game, it was as good a chance as Aberdeen could have hoped for.

But his finish was absolutely awful. Nisbet hesitated when he should have pulled the trigger straight away, allowing Olwethu Makhanya to make a block.

Aberdeen striker Kevin Nisbet reflects on a golden chance to fire Aberdeen ahead at Hampden

On such moments are cup semi-finals won and lost. Just seven minutes later, at the other end of the pitch, Ryan Naderi prodded home from close range to send Rangers through to the final.

Nisbet will surely be haunted by his miss. He has scored 13 goals this season. For all Aberdeen’s struggles, some have even touted him for a Scotland recall.

But he is not up to scratch at the top level. In some respects, he finds himself in the same boat as Lawrence Shankland.

Any time Shankland has been given an opportunity with Scotland, he hasn’t really taken it. Particularly in the World Cup in the summer.

Nisbet is a decent enough striker at Scottish Professional Football League level. But in the big moments in big games, he’s not good enough.

It was a chance he had to take. In the end, Aberdeen were left to rue what might have been as Rangers, who were poor for much of the game, edged through to the final.

All in all, this is a defeat which just piles more pressure on Stephen Robinson. His team did not play poorly but they did not win.

Nisbet took too long with the ball and allowed Olwethu Makhanya the chance to block his shot

There is no sense in trotting out excuses about being competitive and unlucky. Aberdeen were not unlucky.

They had a glorious chance to go in front late in the game and their captain wasted it. That is not misfortune. It is profligacy.

Robinson and his players now face a huge game against Hibs at Pittodrie next Saturday.

With the international break just around the corner, a time when clubs invariably change manager once the rot has set in, it could well be last-chance saloon for Robinson.

#1510. 9 times when Ian Wright was a national treasure: Desert Island discs, Mr Pigden…

You don’t need to be a Crystal Palace or Arsenal fan to love Ian Wright, as our definitive list of why he’s a national treasure demonstrates.

Sure, Wright was a pretty phenomenal goalscorer in his heyday, but more importantly, he just seems like an absolutely brilliant person.

Whenever he appears on our TVs or radios, he makes us smile. Here’s to you, Wrighty…

It’s what Wright was paid to do; he duly obliged and then some, averaging just under a goal every two matches throughout his career.

After six years at Palace – where he bagged 90 goals in 225 appearances – the former England international move to Arsenal for £2.5million in 1991.

It was at Highbury where he would really make his mark. He not only hit the net on his debut in the League Cup against Leicester City but also scored a hat-trick versus Southampton on his league debut and finished the season on 31 goals.

At the Gunners he lifted a Premier League title, two FA Cups, a League Cup and the UEFA Cup Winners’ Cup, finishing at Highbury with 128 goals in 221 appearances – a club record until a certain Thierry Henry came along.

He went on to play for West Ham, where he had a successful loan spell at Nottingham Forest, Celtic and finished his career at Burnley.

The man gave us all hope. Three months short of his 22nd birthday, Wright was still playing for semi-professional outfit Greenwich Borough before Crystal Palace boss Steve Coppell received a tip-off from Billy Smith, the manager of Dulwich Hamlet at the time.

Wright was given a trial at Selhurst Park and never looked back as he earned a professional deal. Before his spell at Greenwich Borough in 1985, Wright had only played for a Sunday league club called Ten-em-Bee.

So ladies and gentlemen, if you’re still waking up early on a Sunday to lace up your boots, just remember: you can still make it.

One of the most heart-warming pieces of footage you are ever likely to see in football. Wright, who had not seen Mr Syd Pidgen for almost 25 years before the clip, was surprised by his former primary school teacher.

Pidgen at the time admitted that Wright probably expected him to have passed away and the former Arsenal striker was visibly emotional to see him.

“You’re alive!” Wright said to him as he broke down and hugged Pidgen. He described his former tutor as the “first main imposing male figure in my life” and “kind of like his special guy”.

And on his appearance on Desert Island Discs, which you really need to listen to, Wright paid further tribute to Mr Pidgen, who has now sadly passed away.

It’s a wonderful man talking about his love for another wonderful man. It’s suddenly got quite dusty in here.

Part of the reason Wright is so likeable is his big smile, charm and self-effacing personality. Most importantly, Wright knows how to laugh at himself and must be one of the most infectious characters in football punditry.

His appearances on the Monday Night Club and 606 with Kelly Cates are his main gigs on the radio, but it’s his TV appearances where he really comes into his own.

Maybe it’s his dazzling white smile or his obvious love of life that comes across more on the box – whatever it is, it’s made for some quality television in recent times.

Here he is with a quick-witted response after Gary Lineker lays a jibe on him:

And Wrighty isn’t one to let someone get away with saying something he doesn’t agree with, especially Robbie Savage…

From the Football Association to Arsenal, Wright is the last person to beat around the bush – if something needs saying, he’s not afraid to say it.

And that’s what fans want. We want to hear proper opinion rather than cliches churned out by pundits that take the game too seriously. Wright makes it fun…

Strong opinions from @IanWright0 on England and the FA. Let’s hear yours & your questions for #askwrighty. On air at 7pm. pic.twitter.com/sqGXeuUfCG

At some point we can’t quite establish, Wright became somewhat of a fashion icon. Well, icon may be taking it a little too far, but he pulls off outfits that we can only wish we were brave enough to attempt.

A post shared by Ian Wright (@wrightyofficial) on Jan 29, 2020 at 4:24am PST

Wright was never a stranger to television, guest starring as a presenter on Top of the Pops back in 2004 before signing up for two seasons of his own chat show on ITV named Friday Night’s All Wright.

#1509. Newcastle: Four potential replacements for Matthias Jaissle after latest defeat

Matthias Jaissle’s status as Newcastle United manager looks very fragile after yet another defeat in which they look tactically lost.

Appointing a man with no Premier League experience raised eyebrows and after some encouraging early results, Newcastle’s blood-and-thunder tactic has been found out and the club have won just one of their last five games.

With Jaissle seemingly out of his depth, there is growing speculation his head could be the first on the Premier League chopping block but the question the Newcastle board have to answer is who do they replace him with?

There are not a lot of options out there either. Eddie Howe is the best prospect for any Premier League club not called Newcastle and barring a dramatic comeback, they will have to look elsewhere.

Here are four candidates they could consider.

Other than Pep Guardiola, Didier Deschamps is the most decorated manager currently out of work.

He left the France role in the summer after 14 years in the job, during which he reached three major wins and won the World Cup.

Deschamps is not without club experience either. He won Ligue 1 with Marseille in the 2009/10 season and was the manager who took Juventus back up from Serie B following the Calciopoli scandal.

He also reached the final of the Champions League with Monaco in 2004 and so certainly has the CV to back it up.

Now the 58-year-old is reported to be looking for a way back into club management with Juventus said to be interested in appointing him.

He may take some convincing though. Going from a World Cup winner to battling in the lower echelons of the Premier League is quite the hard sell but Newcastle may be able to convince him to take on their project.

READ: Newcastle United & 11 more clubs who shamelessly changed their badges for the worse

Nagelsmann’s reputation has taken a bit of a hit following unsuccessful stints at Bayern and Germany and so he may have to rebuild it away from the elite club for now. Enter Newcastle.

The 39-year-old would certainly fit into the sexy manager category and he is one of the more tactically flexible modern coaches. He primarily used a 4-2-3-1 at Bayern and is another proponent of the high-pressing style.

It didn’t work at Germany but that was also to do with a lacklustre generation of talent. It could then work at Newcastle.

McKenna is the obvious name that will get to a lot of jobs with him having the unusual distinction of walking away from his last club rather than getting the sack.

His work at Ipswich has made him one of the highest-rated young managers in England but there is still some doubt about his ability to coach in the Premier League, which he has yet to prove.

He’s a young manager with a lot of potential but Newcastle fans may believe they are past that point in their trajectory.

There is also the fact that McKenna left Ipswich to spend more time away from his family and Newcastle is an awfully long way from his home in Suffolk.

This is the sexy appointment Newcastle fans would love.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea man is the rising young star of the coaching world with his Como side qualifying for the Champions League last season.

But that success is also exactly why it may be hard to get him to Tyneside. Not only is he the manager, he is also a shareholder in the Serie A club and so may find it especially hard to move away at this time.

But Fabregas has been open about his desire to manage in the Premier League and so maybe Newcastle could tempt him.

His style is exactly as you’d expect from an ex-Barcelona and Arsenal man with his teams enjoying the majority of possession and focused on high pressing, the latter of which was an Eddie Howe staple.

He plays with a 4-2-3-1 which is what Newcastle use now and so there would not be too much adapting needing to be done. Crucially, he also knows the league having made 350 appearances in it which is 350 more than Jaissle made.

#1508. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target back in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernández-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment taskforce “the one”.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1507. Man Utd & Forest shocking in 2026-27 Premier League wage bill vs. position comparison

Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal are all sitting in vastly contrasting places when you compare their wage bill rankings to their league positions after the first four games of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

Of course, it’s still early in the season. Nine matches can tell us only so much about how the season will eventually play out, and the table is still taking shape.

Still, there are already some big, eye-catching differences between wage outlay and performance.

Brighton lead the way. They are third in the Premier League despite having the 15th-highest wage bill, which stands at just £51million. That is a remarkable +12 difference between their league position and wage ranking.

Brentford are second in that regard. They are sixth while ranking 17th for wages, with a £49million annual bill, giving them a +11 difference. Hull City are third, sitting 11th despite having the 19th-highest wage bill at just £16million. Their +8 difference is another remarkable return for a newly-promoted side.

Leeds United have also made an impressive start. They occupy 12th place while sitting 14th in the wage rankings. Their annual wage bill is only £53million, giving them a +2 difference.

Ipswich are another side punching well above their wage bill. They sit 14th while ranking 18th for wages, with an annual wage bill of just £20million. That’s a +4 difference.

The traditional powerhouses have produced a mixed bag. Arsenal are top while having the third-highest wage bill in the division, at £154million. That puts them two places ahead of their wage position, while Manchester City are second and second in the wage rankings, exactly matching their wage ranking.

Chelsea are fourth with the seventh-highest wage bill, £97million, while top spenders Liverpool are fifth. The Reds have the highest wage bill in the Premier League at £177million but sit four places below that ranking.

The other ‘Big Six’ underachievers are not hard to spot. Manchester United are 17th with the fourth-highest wage bill of £152million, while Tottenham are ninth despite having the fifth-highest at £138million. Oof.

Villa are also slightly off the pace. They are 10th despite having the sixth-highest wage bill, with £98million going on salaries. That puts them four places below their wage ranking.

We’ve ranked every Premier League club by the gap between their league position and wage-bill ranking, from the biggest overperformers to the biggest underperformers. Keep an eye on this one, as we’ll be keeping it updated as the season progresses.

Note: All wage bill data is via Capology.

League Position: 19 Wage Bill Ranking: 10 Annual wage bill: £64m Difference: -9

League Position: 18 Wage Bill Ranking: 9 Annual wage bill: £66m Difference: -9

#1506. RANGERS 1 ABERDEEN 0: Ryan Naderi the Hampden hero as Light Blues squeeze past dogged Dons to reach final

Published: 16:41 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EDT, 31 October 2026

Ryan Naderi is developing the happy knack of turning up in the right place at the right time for Rangers. And, by Jove, how they needed him to deliver something to break the deadlock in this one and book a spot in the Premier Sports Cup final back at Hampden next month.

Derek McInnes’ side weren’t as bad at the national stadium as they were midweek in scraping a 2-2 draw away to Hearts, but they certainly weren’t all that good. Aberdeen turned up to frustrate them last night and succeeded for the large part, making a number of notable chances themselves.

There’s an obligation to drop in some kind of pun about Hallowe’en in this account of what went down between these two sides, so let's discuss how Dons’ captain Kevin Nisbet must have spent last night suffering nightmares following his own personal horror show just 14 minutes from time.

With the game back hanging in the balance in the wake of a strong period of Rangers pressure, Stephen Robinson’s side broke forward in numbers and, even after Nisbet had failed to find substitute Mitchy Ntelo with a pass, the ball was picked up by Stuart Armstrong and fed back into the skipper’s path on the right-hand side of the box.

He had to smash it first-time. Hard and low across the keeper. Inexplicably, for a guy who does know how to find the net and has done it plenty of times throughout his career, he took a touch and allowed Olwethu Makhanya the opportunity to get across and put in a crucial block.

In that instant, you wondered if the Dons’ big chance had come and gone. Naderi provided the answer just seven minutes later.

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi celebrates his late semi-final winner at Hampden Park

Rangers boss Derek McInnes enjoys the moment at full-time as his side are through to the final

The Czech internationalist endured a grim start to the season as a lone frontman, but has come into his own since being deployed beside Kevin Kelsy and shown that precious ability to score goals that really change things, really matter.

He scored the winner at Celtic Park in September, of course, as well as a home winner against Motherwell. Last time out against St Johnstone, his second-half effort to notch the second goal of what ended up a 4-0 romp was expertly timed as his team-mates had failed to wake up at the start of the second 45 and looked like they might fall flat on their faces.

Once again, he rode to the rescue here, reading the play, making a run, getting into space and finishing from close-in for his eighth of the campaign. The kind of bread-and-butter goal you want your strikers to score.

A cross in from the left from Rangers’ best player Badredine Bouanani, turning up on the wrong wing for some reason, was cleared by Connor Ronan to substitute Dan Neil 25 yards out.

His short pass to James Penrice resulted in a low shot into the area and Naderi timed his run perfectly to ghost in and convert from close range.

It was a sickening blow to under-pressure Robinson and his players. They had dug in really well, pulled off the game plan nicely and kept themselves in it throughout. Their display belied the league form that has put the manager’s job on the line ahead of next Saturday’s teatime visit of Hibernian.

It all counts for nothing in the end, though. As they reflect on events in Mount Florida, they will know that they came up against a Rangers side that most definitely dominated possession — and probably deserved the win in the end — but was vulnerable at times and failed to function as McInnes would have wanted.

The Ibrox boss pulled something of a surprise in his starting line-up by dropping vice-captain Neil and putting left-back Penrice in beside skipper-for-the-night Nico Raskin. It didn’t really work, though.

Listen, those guys weren’t exactly the core of the problem. A lot of the time, the ball wasn’t even being played through midfield, but the switch-up just didn’t feel like it worked. The balance wasn’t right.

For most of the first half, in particular, not very much was right about Rangers. They had plenty of the ball but Aberdeen set up in a 5-3-2 formation and kept them quiet while managing to create good chances of their own on the counter-attack.

Rangers were too slow. Not creative enough. Everything truly positive and dangerous they did went through Badredine Bouanani on the right, but there has to be infinitely more variation in their play rather than just getting it to the on-loan Algerian and hoping those quick feet of his can work some magic.

It was heartbreak for Aberdeen's Nicky Devlin as they fell just short in the semi-final

When he was brought in from German side VfB Stuttgart, the chat was that the management team saw him as an ideal weapon to break down teams playing a low block. He has the ability to beat a man, play in tight spots, have a shot.

However, there’s got to be more about Rangers than that. In this game, as with the 2-2 midweek draw with Hearts at Tynecastle, there just wasn’t enough in the way of fluent, purposeful play. They’ve looked nothing like the side that blew St Johnstone away last weekend with some exhilarating football and that must be a worry for McInnes.

By this stage of the season, they should be starting to find their stride, develop more in the way of consistency.

It took Rangers 44 minutes, for example, to fashion a shot on target. Naturally, it came from Bouanani, a low effort from a central position being saved low to his right by Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Muller.

Up until that point, the better of the opportunities had fallen to the Dons. Midway through the opening period, Raskin played a pass wide to Dujon Sterling that carried just too much jeopardy.

Nesta Guinness-Walker nipped in to steal possession and then took the ball for a run all the way into the final third before releasing a decent low effort which Ibrox No1 Ivor Pandur had to save to his left.

With ten minutes of the half to play, Nisbet then sent a header wide from a great position after moving onto a cross from Brad Lyons.

At that stage, all Rangers had to shout about was an appeal for a penalty turned down on the 16-minute mark when Dons striker Ayoub Mouloua clearly handled the ball in his own area under pressure from Manny Fernandez.

Referee Ryan Lee didn’t give the award with VAR John Beaton backing up that call. It was controversial and no mistake.

Towards the end of the first half, however, it looked like things might be starting to click for McInnes’ men. Naderi put a header just over from a Raskin cross after getting in behind Jack Milne and Min-su Kim, massively disappointing again and eventually replaced by Djeidi Gassama, sliced an effort wide directly in front of goal.

Yet, it remained stodgy for Rangers after the restart. In the wake of Naderi just failing to get on the end of a low shot from Bouanani at the back post, a deflected Nisbet shot at the other end had to be saved low and smartly by Pandur.

Kelsy missed a sitter just after the hour when putting a header miles wide from a brilliant Bouanani cross and Muller had to block a shot from the Algerian wide man with his right boot as Rangers enjoyed their most dangerous and insistent period of the match.

It didn’t last, but Nisbet dallied when it mattered while Naderi just let his instinct take control for a sharp little conversion from that Penrice effort.

McInnes now has his first shot at silverware as Rangers manager pending and that’s what he wanted going into this game.

However, he needs to find a way to get this team slicker, tighter, more joined-up. More relentless. More focused. More composed in key areas.

As if a reminder of that was needed, it came in time added-on when Armstrong picked up the ball at the edge of their box and bent a fine effort just wide of Pandur’s left-hand post.

So near and yet so far. The story of Aberdeen’s night, really. A night where a big chance definitely existed, but just couldn’t be taken.

#1505. Premier League table vs squad cost 2026-27: Man Utd are the biggest underachievers…

We are nine games into the Premier League season. Who are the biggest underperformers and overachievers? Manchester United and Hull City, in particular, make for an interesting contrast when you compare their league position with how much their squads cost to assemble.

While squad cost is not a direct assessment of how a team should perform, it does give us an idea of where they should be aiming for.

With that in mind, we’ve taken the current Transfermarkt valuation of each Premier League squad cost and compared it to where each team currently finds itself in the table.

And boy, does it make Manchester United look bad. United are 17th in the Premier League table after nine games despite having the fifth-most expensive squad in the division, giving them a 12-place disparity between their squad cost position and their actual league position.

That’s miles worse than even the likes of Nottingham Forest and Newcastle, who this table doesn’t exactly make pretty reading for either.

At the other end of the scale, Hull are 11th despite having the cheapest squad in the division. That puts them nine places above where their squad cost would suggest they might be expected to be.

Everton are also punching well above their weight, sitting seventh despite ranking 16th for squad cost. Their +9 difference matches Hull’s, while Brighton (+6), Leeds (+5), Arsenal (+5) and Brentford (+4) have also outperformed their squad cost rankings.

Manchester City, meanwhile, are second in the Premier League while having the second-most expensive squad according to Transfermarkt, meaning their league position is exactly in line with their squad cost ranking.

#1504. Stats not good enough! Derek McInnes issues warning to his Rangers players over their profligacy in front of goal

Published: 18:38 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:47 EDT, 31 October 2026

Rangers manager Derek McInnes last night warned his side they have to ramp up the killer instinct in front of goal after branding their attacking stats in the one-goal Premier Sports Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen ‘embarrassing’.

The Ibrox outfit had 25 shots on goal with only five on target at the end of a Hampden tussle settled by a close-range finish from striker Ryan Naderi with just seven minutes left to play.

McInnes feels his players are making too many bad decisions in the final third of the field and has told wide men such as Badredine Bouanani and Kim Min-su, who has yet to record an assist or goal this term, that they need to start pitching in with better figures.

He accepts there is a lack of top-level experience among a group of attackers notable for their youth, but knows there must be improvements in the quest for silverware.

‘We came with the intention of making sure we got the club into a cup final by hook or by crook, and we’ve done the job, so I am really pleased and delighted with the players, in the main, for their perseverance, for keeping going,’ said McInnes.

‘Semi-finals aren’t easy to get through, particularly when you play the way we did in the first half.

Derek McInnes labelled his team's attacking statistics 'embarrassing' after their Hampden win

‘We were ponderous when we needed to be quicker. When we needed to be calm in the final bit, we snatched and made poor decisions.

‘In terms of the stats, it is actually embarrassing we have had 25 shots and only five on target. It says a lot about the inexperience at the top end of the pitch.

‘That’s for another day. Today was just all about getting through. It’s so important for the club and the supporters to look forward to a cup final.

‘We need to keep arriving in cup finals and get the job done to win trophies.

‘I always feel there’s goals in us,’ said the Ibrox boss. ‘Equally, I was still a bit concerned on counter-attacks. Aberdeen had a couple of moments that gave them oxygen and belief that maybe they could get in the final, but the better team won.

‘Naderi, like all good strikers, is going that way when the defenders are on their heels and he gets these scruffy goals that you want your striker to score.

‘He’s always in the middle of the goal when the ball gets into good areas, but a lot of the time we don’t feed him enough. We make too many bad decisions.

Kevin Kelsy watches a header fly wide on a rare off night for the Venezuelan front man

‘Some of the stats that we’re seeing more or less every week at the minute, it’s like making poor decisions, snatching at things, rushing crosses, not making the right pass, not putting the extra pass in. I’m going to keep saying that we’re a young team up there and it’s hard sometimes.

‘You need an old man up there, an old head, nous, who knows just how to bring a bit of savvy and calmness to it.

‘Thankfully, we had that with the goal today, but there were so many other times where we could, if we just take more care, be less rushed and stay calm in those moments, create better opportunities rather than just 25 shots and 20 of them flying over the bar.

‘Those shots on target become double, triple more of what we get, and it’s those wee bits that we need to sharpen up if we’re going to be successful this season.’

Asked if he felt there would be more goals in man-of-the-match Bouanani, McInnes replied: ‘There had better! The wide players need to start scoring goals.

‘Min-su needs to get that demand on himself, Gassama. Bouanani’s got so much quality.

‘The thing with Bouanani is, as soon as he steps on the pitch on that left side, 25 yards out, you think it’s in the net because he does it time and time again in training. If he keeps chapping at the door, I’m sure the goals will come.

‘I’d like to have enjoyed this a wee bit more. Enjoyment comes now, a wee bit of satisfaction when I see the lads in the dressing room celebrating together, but the job now is to go and win the thing.

Badredine Bouanani goes close with a curling effort but McInnes wants to see more from him

‘We’ll get six weeks now between now and then where we need to get better at things I just spoke about.

‘We’re on a really strong run just now in terms of wins and being unbeaten over a period of time, but we know we’re not perfect. It’s important that we keep searching for those improvements.’

Naderi lapped up his eighth goal of the season and insisted the right team won.

‘It was wonderful. I am so happy. It was a wonderful second half and we deserved it. It was just a question of time until we scored,’ said Naderi.

‘We had so many corners back-to-back, so much pressure, so many shots on target.’

Captain-for-the-night Nico Raskin, meanwhile, agreed with McInnes’ view that the team has to become more ruthless in front of goal.

‘Their goalkeeper made loads of saves and we could maybe have been a bit more calm in front of goal, but I am just so happy for Ryan and the team we got the goal,’ he said.

‘It is about trying to be more clinical now and enjoying the game more as it is always tense at 0-0 or 1-0. We want to come back to Hampden and win the cup now.’

#1503. Hearts keeper Reus hopes to use inside knowledge of his old boss Reedijk to prolong Hibs manager's false start as they clash in derby

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 18:43 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 18:49 EDT, 31 October 2026

When Hibs appointed Marink Reedijk just over a month ago, there weren’t many people within Scottish football who could claim to know much about the Dutchman.

Especially among the Hibs support, the response was one largely of bemusement as to why the club had taken a gamble on a 34-year-old rookie whose only previous experience was in the Belgian second tier.

At Beveren, Reedijk carved a reputation for himself as a coach who played high-octane attacking football as his side finished last season unbeaten as champions, duly winning promotion to the top flight.

It was an achievement and a style of play which was sufficiently impressive enough to alert the data boffins at Jamestown Analytics.

Back in the summer, Reedijk’s name had actually been on Hearts’ radar before they eventually chose to appoint Wouter Vrancken instead.

There was never any formal approach, but Hearts and Jamestown were aware of his name and his reputation as a young coach of considerable promise.

Whether or not Reedijk’s style of play could translate to the SPFL Premiership was a topic of much intrigue when he arrived to replace the sacked David Gray.

Reus denies Martin Boyle back in September's Edinburgh derby meeting

It is fair to say he has made something of an inauspicious start. In beginning his reign with defeats to Dundee United, Falkirk and Celtic, he became the first Hibs boss since Pat Fenlon to lose his opening three games.

He finally arrested that sequence courtesy of a 1-1 draw against St Mirren in midweek, but Hibs remain mired in relegation trouble.

Now comes the small matter of an Edinburgh derby against Hearts, with the rivals set to clash at Hampden this afternoon in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup.

Reedijk desperately needs a victory to finally ignite his reign, with many Hibs fans already questioning whether this is a gamble that may backfire.

In the 2-1 defeat to Celtic last weekend, Hibs finished the match with Grant Hanley playing up front for the final ten minutes. It was an act of desperation and one which would see Reedijk take a lot of criticism.

Yet, although Reedijk is struggling to convince so far, there’s a man behind enemy lines who will happily sing his praises.

Reedijk picked up his first point as Hibs boss in the midweek draw at St Mirren

Hearts goalkeeper Beau Reus played under Reedijk for two years at Beveren. Reus insists he would be happy to go out on a limb and vouch that his old boss is a top-class operator.

As is always the way in football, friends can be found in unlikely places. Prior to a Hampden derby showdown, Reus opened up on his relationship with his fellow Dutchman during their time in Belgium.

‘We were together in Belgium the last two years,’ said the Hearts keeper, who has been excellent since making the switch to Tynecastle. ‘For me, he’s a good manager. His gameplan is really clear.

‘Hopefully that helps us a bit to crack the code. I will have a meeting with our coach to tell him how he will play, probably!

‘But Marink is very adaptable. He’s a young coach. I know he will have some tricks up his sleeve.

‘We are both Dutch and, as always, if you are a guy from an outside country that plays in Belgium, it’s normal you have a certain connection. He helped me grow a lot.

‘He’s really straight, so if he has a plan, he will go to implement his plan as well as he can. Off the pitch he’s a really, really nice guy, really warm. But, yeah, as soon as you’re on the pitch with him, you know exactly what you have to do for him. He makes very clear.

‘We are very kind to each other, but I think on Sunday we will forget about it for 90 minutes. After that, we can shake hands again.

‘I knew there were rumours that he was coming to Hibs, so the day I left for the last international break, I flew back to Amsterdam and his plane was just landing.

‘I said to my girlfriend it’s unbelievable that I come across him again in this way. But in football it is always like this, you will see each other many times.’

Reus is impressing for Hearts, with his shootout heroics securing a Conference League spot

Hearts come into the semi-final on the back of a 2-2 draw against Rangers at Tynecastle on Wednesday night, a match in which they were the better side for large spells.

Vrancken’s men are battling through an injury crisis which currently sees eight first-team regulars out of action.

‘It is devastating when you see so many injuries,’ noted Reus. ‘But we will play with the players we have and give 100 per cent for sure.’

It promises to be a thriller in Mount Florida as Reedijk’s Hibs go up against Vrancken’s Hearts. Two coaches renowned for front-foot attacking football, it’ll be anything but dull.

Reus insists it would be a major sign of the continued progress being made at Hearts if they can reach the final.

‘I don’t know the numbers off the top of my head, but the last time the club won this competition was quite some time ago,’ he said. ‘So it’s massive.

‘And of course, it’s always great to play for cups, playing in tournaments, because you don’t win that many trophies in your career, so every chance is one.

‘The fact it is a derby is great. We have already played Hibs before this season and beaten them at Easter Road.

‘You see how much tension and how much build-up there was to the game. Also in the stadium, how much they hated us! So, if you win, it’s extra nice.

‘It is another massive game and we really want to bounce back from the disappointment of losing the late goal against Rangers in midweek.’

#1502. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

Published: 16:49 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 19:55 EDT, 31 October 2026

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to be on the verge of tears as he embraced the travelling faithful following his side's latest defeat.

Fernandes returned to the United side after being dropped for their loss against Bournemouth last week, when he was an unused substitute.

The decision from Michael Carrick came after his skipper had criticised Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, leading to uncertainty around the duo's relationship.

In the week, however, they held crisis talks to fix their relationship, and Fernandes was back in the team – and playing 90 minutes – against Chelsea on Saturday.

Yet he was unable to turn around his side's fortunes, with United falling to a 2-0 defeat, and the club have now gone nine games in all competitions without a win.

And he appeared to be in a battle to hold back the tears as United's players headed over to the away end at full-time, showing how much the team's poor form is affecting him.
