Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. But the Arsenal man hesitates and the keeper spreads himself, blocking Madueke’s eventual shot. He can’t turn around to get on the rebound and cuts is back for Tzolis, whose own shot is then blocked.

With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

Rice loses the ball in midfield and fouls Olivera as he tries to recover it.

Before they take the free kick though, Arsenal make more changes. Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke come on for Gyokeres and Saka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Sums up the game so far really for Arsenal.

There is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

There are the subs, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are the ones to make way.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

At the same time, Favasuli makes a neat little run on the right trying to get to the touchline and pull the ball back, but Raya is able to pick it up easily.

That was almost it for Napoli, Hojlund with a great run in behind. He gets into the box one-on-one against his defender as Raya retreats. The challenge is perfectly timed though as he tries to get his shot off and the ball goes spinning off to the side.

Neither side are looking clinical in front of goal though as Arsenal take the ball down the other end, and Declan Rice can only send another shot over the bar.

Saka tries to take another chance on the edge of the box, but he loses the ball.

Napoli try to seize their moment on the break, with Favasuli releasing down the left side. He looks for Hojlund in the middle of the field, but his cross is just not good enough and Raya comes out to collect the high ball.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

Though the hosts came out on the front foot, it has been all Arsenal since then, so Allegri will be hoping these changes can shift the momentum.

Alisson Santos gets past White on the sideline, and makes the run down the left. He tries to find De Bruyne making the run in the middle but it is intercepted and Arsenal take the ball back up the field.

Napoli are getting ready to make some changes.

Arsenal probing again, with Rice, Saka, Odegaard and White exchanging passes on the right edge of the box. Saka tries a low ball in but it’s blocked before it gets to Gyokeres.

Napoli are sitting so deep, you have to assume they are just waiting for an opportunity to counter. Even so, Arsenal are doing well to keep the ball moving around and try and find space. The hosts are really trying not to concede first.

Another wasted chance for Arsenal! Great play from Odegaard lifting a little ball into the centre of the box, which is flicked on towards goal. It falls to Hincapié in the six-yard box but as he tries to poke it into the goal, the Ecuadorian sends it flying over the bar.

Napoli have every man behind the ball right now as Arsenal get some possession.

Arsenal’s turn now, as White gets himself into a good position on the right side of the box, exchanging passes with Odegaard and Saka.

Saka tries to send a ball into the box, but it’s blocked and sent out the sideline as Napoli remain disciplined and shut down the space.

That momentum falls apart for Napoli as Oliveira fouls Gyokeres as the strikers comes in to defend.

Napoli are starting with some pressure here..

Napoli have changed their keepers at half-time. Meret received some treatment in the first half and has been taken off, replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. It’s his first appearance of the season.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

Reigning champions PSG are 3-0 up against Slovan, with a quick double coming from Mr Ballon D’or himself, Ousmane Dembélé. Ferran Torres scored the third.

Sporting vs Galatasaray also level at 1-1 so it’s really all to play for in the next 45 minutes. Stay tuned!

That’s the final action of the half, and nothing separates the two sides at the break. Both with three shots on target, though Arsenal have taken 13 shots to Napoli’s four.

Both teams could have stolen a goal to take the lead, but they will have to wait for the second period for the opportunity.

Arsenal get a corner which is delivered really well to the far post, but as it’s headed in, there is no space for White to turn and shoot from the six-yard box. He tries to lay it off for Hincapié but Meret gets low to grab it.

Arsenal have created more than enough chances to be three or four goals clear here. That miss by Saka was the best one yet, and the England winger will be in disbelief at the spooned nature of his finish. It looked a certain goal. Shocker.

Arsenal get another great chance as Odegaard sends a perfect ball to Saka as he makes the run into the box on the right side. The winger stays onside but Lobotka does enough to put him off and Saka sends it over the bar.

Napoli are first into the book as Gilmour fouls Eze 35 yards out.

Arsenal take the free kick but end up passing the ball around the edge of the box. Eventually Odegaard lifts a high ball into the box, but Meret punches it away confidently.

Konsa does really well to hold up Alisson Santos as he makes a very speedy run down the left, keeping him from sending a ball into the box.

The game is opening up now, as Saka makes a run of his own down the right, with Gyokeres in the box but Napoli keep tight and Rrahmani does well to stop the ball reaching the striker.

A good save from Raya as Hojlund again feeds the wings from the centre of the field. Politano makes a great run in from the right side with the ball and takes a curling shot with his left foot on the edge of the box.

Arsenal’s keeper collects and then minutes later his side have a shot of their own, but Saka can only send it over the bar.

Saka again gets enough time on the right edge of the box to send a low ball to Rice in the right corner. His shot goes over the bar and we’re having an impromptu drinks break as Meret gets some treatment.

Treat yourself to a hydration break of your own.

Napoli coming close as Hojlund fed in the centre, one-on-one with Konsa, trying to turn at the top of the box. He dinks the ball into the path of the running De Bruyne, whose shot is blocked by Konsa, who scrambles back quickly.

Hincapié sends a cross in from the left which almost catches Meret out at the near post as the keeper scrambles across to push it away.

Now it’s Napoli’s turn as Lobotka sends a long ball down the left to Alisson Santos, who sends a great cross in to the box. Konsa just does enough to put him off and it meets Rice in the centre of the box, for the midfielder to clear.

Saka comes in again on his left foot, with a series of short passes between Odegaard and Rice, but his shot is blocked as two defenders shut him down.

Another attempt for Arsenal as Odegaard gets forward and passes to Eze on the left wing. He drives in and takes a shot with his right foot from just inside the box, but he drags it wide of the target.

Good start to this game. Plenty going on. Arsenal look dangerous and capable of pinning Napoli deep into their own half, but the Italians have threatened on the break. De Bruyne’s shot from range would have triggered some nasty flashbacks for the Arsenal fans but, thankfully for them, it was straight at Raya.

Great chance from Arsenal as Eze pulls away at the back post and connects with the ball to send a header into the box. Merino connects with a diving header of his own but it’s straight at Meret and tipped over the bar.

Arsenal again biding their time until Rice plays a neat ball to White on the right edge of the boxm which he lifts into the box. No one around to do anything with it and Meret collects.

Arsenal being patient on the edge of the box moving the ball around, but eventually it breaks down with Eze losing the ball and then fouling De Bruyne as he tries to break away.

The Napoli players feel that should have been a card.

Di Lorenzo again looks to find space down the centre of the field but sends the ball out to Politano again on the right wing, who lofts a very high ball towards the back post but Raya collects with confidence.

Di Lorenzo makes a great run onto a long ball on the left side, racing down the sideline. He sends a ball across to find De Bruyne in the centre of the field, and the midfielder takes a great shot, which Raya can’t hold on to. White reacts to clear but Napoli are having a good spell.

Politano is the next to force a save from the Arsenal keeper with a shot from the right corner of the box, keeping their visitors very much on their toes.

Arsenal dominating possession in the early stages, just testing the Napoli defence. The stadium is quite quiet and we can hear the travelling fans declaring their love for their team.

Free kick for the visitors as Eze is fouled 40 yards out. Odegaard takes and sends a high ball into the centre of the box, which Gabriel can’t quite control.

Arsenal come again as Gyokeres sends a cross into the box from the left and Saka tries an overhead kick but it is straight into the centre of the goal and Meret has little trouble.

Rice again but the keeper comes to collect and sets the counter free.

Hojlund makes a great run and feeds Alisson Santos on the left side. He tries to cut in but is well marked by White and he can only send his shot over the bar from inside the box.

Arsenal get their first corner as Eze finds himself in a central position at the top of the box, and plays neat one-two with Gyokeres, but his shot takes a big deflection.

Rice goes to the corner flag, and sends in a good ball, headed out by Napoli for another corner.

Arsenal probing on the right wing, with White, Odegaard and Saka overlapping nicely. The captain feeds White and he passes in a neat little ball to Saka just inside the box. He tries a shot, but it’s blocked.

Napoli are getting back very quickly when Arsenal are pressing.

Marín sends a nice high ball across the field to find Politano on the right side. He feeds De Bruyne on the edge of the box and the Belgian tries a shot at Raya, curling it with his right foot, but with not much on it, Raya collects in the middle of goal.

Both teams getting little spells on the ball to get going.

Arsenal are keeping tight as Napoli try and play the ball out from the back and the long ball out to Hojlund is easily collected for Raya.

You can hear the Arsenal fans in loud voice, accompanied by plenty of jeers and whistles from the home fans.

“Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

“We have to turn over a new leaf. We face a different challenge tomorrow. We’ll need to put in a technically excellent performance and be able to defend better than we did against Como and Inter.”

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

“It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Here is how the hosts are lining up tonight:

Meret; Olivera, Marin, Rrahmani, Di Lorenzo; De Bruyne, Lobotka, Gilmour; Santos, Hojlund, Politano

Subs: Favasuli, Badiashile, Neres, Contini, Lucca, Vergara, Beukema, Milinkovic-Savic, Spinazzola

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

Good evening from a very sticky and humid Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, where the temperature is just a little too high to be pleasant. Perhaps that will change in time for kick-off. Perhaps it’s not relevant if I feel a bit uncomfortable in my jeans. Readers can make their own minds up on that…

Anyway, this should be a fun game. The atmosphere is usually pretty intense in this part of the world and they will be up for this one. The absence of Scott McTominay due to a minor heart problem is good news for Arsenal, who are likely to make a few changes to the team that beat Chelsea so impressively at the weekend.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a new attempt to claim their white whale.

Their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they currently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

Despite the carnage at UK airports this week, Sam Dean has made it to Naples and will be bringing us updates from the continent.

#1476. Liverpool vs Arsenal - Premier League RECAP: Mikel Arteta finally wins at Anfield to take his side three points clear at the top after perfect game plan with Kai Havertz's first-half goal the difference

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Relive Daily Mail Sport's coverage of Arsenal's first win at Anfield in the Premier League for 14 years.

After 14 years of pain at Anfield, Arsenal have finally managed to secure three points at this stadium.

Was it easy? Far from it. Liverpool threw almost everything at the Gunners' defence in what was an electric performance at times from the hosts.

But Mikel Arteta's side showed incredible heart, putting in a defensive masterclass to keep the hosts at bay.

It means the defending champions have gone three points clear at the top of the Premier League, and good luck trying to catch them.

Anyway, I'm now heading for a cheeky rest after what was a breathtaking evening on Merseyside. Thanks for joining us and we will see you all soon.

Mikel Arteta, Arsenal boss, speaking on Sky Sports:

On whether this is a big win in the title race:

Is it time for this conversation again? I think it is.

We are nine games into this Premier League season and Arsenal have already kept six clean sheets and have conceded just five goals.

Remember, three of those goals came in their shock defeat away at Brighton. Bar that odd afternoon, barely anybody has been able to break that rock-solid defence down.

The famous goals conceded record from Chelsea's 2004-05 has been deemed impossible to break. 15 goals in 38 games is just outrageous, isn't it?

But if anybody is capable of breaking that record is this Arsenal team, they are just so hard to score against.

Maybe this is the year they break it? A long way to go, mind.

Declan Rice's statistics against Liverpool:

Daniel Sturridge, former Liverpool striker, on Sky Sports:

Andoni Iraola, Liverpool boss, speaking to Sky Sports:

On whether Alexander Isak should have had a penalty:

Andoni Iraola has a real problem on his hands.

Trey Nyoni's performance today showed why he needs to start every game for them now. He dictated the game from deep, winning a midfield battle against Bruno Guimaraes and Declan Rice.

Nyoni's 53 passes were the most during the 59 minutes he was on the pitch, while he also had the highest pass accuracy in 96 per cent and made the most line-breaking passes with 14.

After he came off, Liverpool lost their momentum.

Dominik Szoboszlai is clearly a fantastic footballer who has produced so many big moments for the Reds over the past few years, but he doesn't quite suit this system.

The Hungarian works incredibly hard but also slows Liverpool's game down. He was taking two or three touches on the ball before making each of his passes.

I think Iraola needs to commit to a Mac Allister and Nyoni midfield behind Wirzt because it clearly works. But that does mean keeping the likes of Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch out of the team.

Arsenal couldn't have hoped for a much better start to the season than they have had.

Their 24 points are the most by a team after nine games of a Premier League season since the Gunners themselves in 2022-23 (also 24).

Only in 2004-05 and 2007-08 have they ever had more at this stage of a PL campaign (25 in both).

It's very much a catch us if you can scenario now.

Now, this isn't a post bashing Liverpool because they played rather well. But I guess I am about to...

I still can't believe that the Reds didn't manage to register a single shot on target, despite applying so much pressure on the Arsenal goal.

It's the first time EVER that a Liverpool side have failed to have a shot on target in a Premier League match at Anfield. That's a crazy stat.

In fact, Liverpool have scored just four goals at Anfield in the Premier League this season, their joint-fewest after five home matches in a top-flight campaign (also four in 1913-14 and 2012-13).

That is something Liverpool need to sort out, and if they do, they will be a proper team.

Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool captain, speaking to Sky Sports:

On whether Alexander Isak should have got a penalty:

I didn't talk about the penalty incident at half-time because I didn't have time, but now I do.

Alexander Isak should have had a penalty. I have no idea how both the referee and VAR saw Jurrien Timber's shirt tug on the striker and didn't give a spot kick.

Just watch the video below; Timber's tug literally stops Isak from connecting with his header. If Isak connected, he may well have found the back of the net.

Isak could have maybe given a bigger reaction, but as everybody has already said, the Swede shouldn't need to.

#1475. Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity1,2,3,4,5,6,7, but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8) and Il1b. Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil–NLRP3–IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1+CD4+ T helper type 17 (TH17) cells9,10. After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung TH17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

Obesity alters immune function across multiple contexts, including infection, autoimmunity and cancer7,12,13,14,15,16,17. This effect is especially pronounced in the skin, where obesity exacerbates inflammation and complicates therapeutic responses6,18. Although chronic obesity and weeks to months of obesogenic diet exposure are known to remodel cutaneous immunity, these longer interventions also produce cumulative metabolic, endocrine, microbial and tissue remodelling across multiple organ systems7. It remains unclear whether comparatively brief, days-scale dietary exposures, before such systemic remodelling is established, can acutely modify triggered inflammatory responses and durably imprint long-term tissue inflammatory memory. Experimental models of acute type 17 skin inflammation provide an opportunity to examine these effects, as psoriasis, a type 17 inflammatory disease tightly linked to obesity4,15, has also been associated with dietary patterns and other nutritional exposures19,20,21. We therefore examined whether transient dietary state could bidirectionally modify the response to a synchronized inflammatory trigger, such that HFD amplifies inflammation in lean mice whereas LFD restrains inflammation in obese mice, and whether this acute dietary window could alter subsequent tissue inflammatory recall.

To distinguish the impact of diet itself from the consequences of established obesity, we used topical imiquimod (IMQ) challenge as a synchronized model of acute type 17 skin inflammation in which age-matched mice were fed either a short-term (1 week) or long-term (10 weeks) HFD (60% kcal from fat), or a low-fat (control) diet (LFD; 10% kcal from fat), before topical IMQ challenge22 (Fig. 1a). Mice remained on their assigned diets throughout IMQ challenge. Measurements of serum cytokine levels before application of IMQ did not reveal significant differences between the three groups (Extended Data Fig. 1a), although we did observe modestly increased numbers of TH17 cells and γδ T cells in the skin of mice fed a short- and long-term HFD, relative to the mice fed LFD (Extended Data Fig. 1b–d). Both short- and long-term HFD also reduced glucose tolerance, although these effects were more pronounced in obese mice that were fed a long-term HFD (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b).

a,f, IMQ model schematics with either HFD (a) or LFD (f) feeding for the indicated durations. b,g, The body weight of mice after HFD (b) or LFD (g) feeding for the indicated durations before IMQ challenge. c,h, The change in ear thickness over the course of disease development in the HFD (c) and LFD (h) groups. d,e,i,j, Representative gross ear images (HFD (d), LFD (i)) and haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained ear sections (HFD (e), LFD (j)) from mice on day 6 of IMQ treatment. w, weeks. k,l, Schematic of 4 days of HFD feeding restricted to 3 days before disease onset and 1 day after disease onset (HFDin) in lean mice (k) and the corresponding change in ear thickness during disease development (l). m,n, Schematic of the 4 days of LFD feeding restricted to 3 days before disease onset and 1 day after disease onset (LFDin) in obese mice (m) and the corresponding change in ear thickness during disease development (n). Scale bars, 100 µm. Data are mean ± s.e.m. n = 10 (b, c, g, h and n) and n = 5 (l) mice per group. Statistical analysis was performed using Brown–Forsythe and Welch’s analysis of variance (ANOVA) followed by Dunnett’s T3 multiple-comparison test (b, c, g, h, l and n). Only peak ear thickness values were used for statistical testing in c, h, l and n. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001. The diagrams in a, f, k and m were created using BioRender; Jiang, Z. https://BioRender.com/l3wal7h (a), https://BioRender.com/ln9fpc1 (f), https://BioRender.com/6cmulc7 (k), https://BioRender.com/zeduory (m) (2026).

As expected, 10 weeks of HFD caused marked obesity, whereas HFD for 1 week did not (Fig. 1b). Despite this, both regimens exacerbated IMQ-induced skin inflammation comparably, with approximately 2.1-fold (1 week) and 2.3-fold (10 week) increases in ear thickness relative to the LFD-fed mice (Fig. 1c). Gross examination revealed equivalent levels of ear shortening (Fig. 1d), and histological analysis showed dermal and epidermal expansion in both groups (Fig. 1e). Notably, 1 week of feeding on a medium-fat diet (MFD; 45% kcal from fat) was sufficient to exacerbate disease to a similar extent to the HFD (60% kcal from fat) (Extended Data Fig. 2c,d), indicating that neither extreme fat exposure nor established obesity is required to amplify inflammation. Consistently, western diet (WD; 40 kcal% fat; 29 kcal% sucrose) feeding amplified inflammation after IMQ treatment to the same extent as MFD feeding (Extended Data Fig. 2e). Further, WD or HFD feeding alone did not induce overt ear inflammation or increased ear thickness in the absence of IMQ challenge across the time periods examined (Extended Data Fig. 2f,g), indicating that diet-sensitive amplification of IMQ-induced inflammation is experimentally separable from spontaneous diet-associated dermatitis as reported in some prolonged diet-feeding models23,24.

To determine whether systemic metabolic correction was sufficient to blunt diet-amplified inflammation, we treated HFD-fed mice with semaglutide during the acute dietary exposure and IMQ challenge. Semaglutide was pharmacologically active, improving glucose excursion, reducing body weight, lowering circulating insulin and leptin, increasing GLP-1 immunoreactivity in an assay that recognizes semaglutide, and reducing white adipose tissue mass (Extended Data Fig. 3a–h). However, semaglutide did not broadly reduce baseline inflammatory cytokines, alter gross ear or spleen morphology or substantially remodel splenic conventional T (Tconv) cell subsets (Extended Data Fig. 3i–l). After IMQ challenge, semaglutide did not attenuate HFD-amplified ear thickening or lesional TH17 inflammation (Extended Data Fig. 3m–p). Thus, HFD-conditioned inflammatory susceptibility can persist despite GLP-1 receptor agonist-mediated improvement in systemic metabolic parameters.

IMQ-induced inflammation predominantly stimulates type 17 immune responses, characterized by the production of IL-17A, IL-17F and IL-22 by TH17 cells, γδ T cells and other immune cells22,25. Flow cytometry revealed that acute and chronic HFD similarly increased levels of CD4+ Tconv cells expressing RORγt, the lineage-defining TH17 transcription factor, as well as CD4+ Tconv cells competent for IL-17A, IL-17F and IL-22 in lesional skin and draining lymph nodes (Extended Data Figs. 1b and 4a–d). TH22 cells (IL-17A−IL-22+FOXP3−CD4+ T cells) were also increased, although to a lesser extent than TH17 cells (Extended Data Fig. 4e). CD4+ T cell proliferation (Ki-67+) was increased (Extended Data Fig. 4f), whereas the proportion of Treg cells was reduced under both conditions (Extended Data Fig. 4g). Neutrophils, which are prominent cellular effectors of type 17 inflammation26, were elevated after just 1 week of HFD, mirroring the increase observed with chronic HFD (Extended Data Fig. 4h). By contrast, the proportion of cytokine-producing γδ T cells was unchanged, although total γδ T cell numbers increased in HFD-fed mice (Extended Data Fig. 4i,j).

Finally, we examined whether brief withdrawal of dietary fat could mitigate disease in obese mice. Mice fed HFD for 13 weeks were switched to LFD for 1 week before IMQ challenge, and were compared with obese mice maintained on HFD and with lean LFD-fed control mice (Fig. 1f). Despite persistent obesity (>40 g), the mice that were switched to LFD did not develop the enhanced ear thickness observed in obese mice maintained on HFD (Fig. 1g–j). Thus, dietary state at the onset of inflammation, rather than body mass alone, dictates the magnitude of inflammatory responses after acute challenge with IMQ. This result prompted us to test whether dietary exposure within a specific temporal window is sufficient to drive this effect.

To define the temporal dynamics of this response, we examined how the timing of HFD feeding influenced IMQ-induced inflammation. Four days of HFD coincident with disease initiation (HFDin) were sufficient to markedly exacerbate inflammation (Fig. 1k,l and Extended Data Fig. 4k,l). Short-term exposure to 15% (w/v) glucose in water during the same peri-initiation window did not enhance IMQ-induced inflammation (Extended Data Fig. 2h–k), suggesting that increased simple sugar exposure is insufficient to recapitulate the acute inflammatory amplification observed with fat-enriched obesogenic diets. By contrast, HFD provided outside this window (HFDout) did not alter disease severity compared with continuous LFD (Extended Data Fig. 2l). Conversely, switching obese mice to LFD during a similar 4-day window (LFDin) protected them from the heightened inflammation observed in obese mice maintained on HFD (Fig. 1m,n), whereas LFD given outside this window (LFDout) offered no protection (Extended Data Fig. 2m). In a complementary experiment, mice that were fed HFD for 1 week and switched to LFD on the day of IMQ initiation (HFDbefore) developed disease severity comparable to mice maintained on HFD, further narrowing the critical dietary window to the onset of inflammation (Extended Data Fig. 2n). Together, these results establish that dietary state during the peri-initiation window, rather than obesity per se, determines disease severity, and raise the question of which immune compartments translate coincident dietary cues into amplified inflammatory responses.

We next sought to identify the critical immune cell types that enhance disease severity and type 3 inflammation after HFD feeding. To this end, we first used Rag1−/− mice, which lack adaptive immunity but retain innate lymphoid cells27. These mice were resistant to HFD-induced exacerbation of disease severity, suggesting that adaptive lymphocytes are required for this effect (Fig. 2a,b). Given the known role of γδ T cells as major IL-17 producers in the skin and their significant expansion after long-term HFD feeding18, we examined the effects of short-term HFD on Tcrd−/− mice. Notably, HFD-fed Tcrd−/− mice also developed significantly greater disease compared with LFD-fed controls (Fig. 2c), suggesting that γδ T cells are dispensable for the short-term HFD-induced inflammatory exacerbation. By contrast, HFD-fed Tcra−/− mice, which do not develop αβ T cells, did not develop greater disease compared with their LFD counterparts, suggesting that αβ T cells are required for short-term HFD-induced disease exacerbation (Fig. 2d). To further identify the subset within the αβ T cell compartment required for the HFD-enhanced disease severity, we used B2m−/− mice, which are deficient in CD8+ T cells, and MHCIIΔ/Δ (H2-Ab1, H2-Aa, H2-Eb1, H2-Eb2, H2-Ea null) mice, which lack CD4+ T cells. Notably, only CD4+ T cell deficiency resulted in the loss of the exacerbated disease and inflammatory response caused by HFD in wild-type (WT) mice (Fig. 2e,f). To further confirm the essential role of CD4+ T cells in altering disease trajectory in response to HFD, we treated WT mice with IgG or CD4-depleting antibody. CD4 depletion completely abolished the diet-induced difference in disease severity between mice fed LFD and those fed HFD (Extended Data Fig. 5a–d). Notably, in this setting, LFD-fed mice displayed modest ear thickening accompanied by an increase in cutaneous γδ T cells (Extended Data Fig. 5e). We then sought to identify whether the presence of CD4+ T cells, in the absence of other adaptive immune cells, could produce an exaggerated immune response to HFD. We adoptively transferred bulk CD4+ T cells isolated from the spleen of WT mice into Rag1−/− mice and, after homeostatic expansion, provided HFD or LFD for 1 week, followed by IMQ treatment (Fig. 2g). Rag1−/− mice that were transferred with CD4+ T cells had a robust enhancement of IMQ-induced disease after HFD feeding, with elevated numbers of TH17 cells in the skin (Fig. 2h–k). Taken together, these results demonstrate that CD4+ T cells are critical immunological mediators in translating dietary influences into enhanced inflammatory responses in this model of skin inflammation.

For i and k, P values were corrected for multiple comparisons using the Holm–Šídák method. Only peak ear thickness values were tested in a–f, h and n. *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001. The diagram in g was created using BioRender; Jiang, Z. https://BioRender.com/t2usnif (2026).

To further elucidate the mechanism by which short-term HFD feeding influences CD4+ T cells, we systematically profiled the lesional CD4+ T cells from LFD- and HFD-fed mice after IMQ challenge using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). Exploratory analysis revealed two Tconv cell clusters (TH1 and TH17), four distinct Treg cell clusters (proliferating, resident, central and Penk+)28 and a naive cluster (Fig. 2l). The gene-expression heat maps of effector cytokines (Il17a, Il17f, Il22, Ifng and Fasl)29, key transcription factors (Rorc, Tbx21, Foxp3 and Ikzf2)10,30,31, cytokine receptors (Il23r, Il1rl1, Il1r1 and Il2ra)30, markers of proliferation (Mki67, Cdca3, Spc24 and Pclaf), prominent markers of activation, quiescence, tissue residency and memory (Ccr7, Sell, Itgae, Klf2 and Bcl2)6 and Penk28 validated these population assignments (Extended Data Fig. 5f).

Cells from mice that were fed HFD showed marked differences in distribution across the cell populations, particularly in the TH17 cluster (Extended Data Fig. 6a). In TH17 cells, TH17 effector genes such as Il17a, Il17f, Il22, Il23r and Rorc were significantly upregulated in CD4+ T cells from HFD-fed mice (Extended Data Fig. 6b). Furthermore, leveraging published gene signatures associated with TH17 pathogenicity9,31, we found that short-term HFD feeding markedly enhances the pathogenicity of TH17 cells in the skin (Extended Data Fig. 6c). We performed differential gene expression analysis (Extended Data Fig. 6d and Supplementary Table 1) and found that Il1r1 was the most strongly upregulated gene from TH17 cells taken from mice fed HFD, as measured by fold change (Fig. 2m and Extended Data Fig. 6d). These findings were further validated by flow cytometry, which confirmed that HFD feeding significantly increases IL-1R1 expression in CD4+ T cells from lesional skin (Extended Data Fig. 6e). IL-1R1 signalling has been shown to be critical for stabilizing and enhancing type 3 inflammation10,32. CD4+ T cells expressing Il1r1 exhibited increased expression of TH17 effector genes, along with a higher TH17 pathogenicity score (Extended Data Fig. 6f,g). TH17 differentiation involves multiple inflammatory cues, of which the circuitry is well defined in vitro but less well understood in vivo33,34. These findings suggest that IL-1R1 has a specific and critical role in driving TH17 differentiation in mice being fed HFD.

To directly test this hypothesis, we subjected mice with T cell-specific ablation of IL-1R1 (Cd4creIl1r1fl/fl) to 1 week of LFD or HFD feeding followed by IMQ challenge. Notably, T cell-specific IL-1R1-deficient mice were completely protected from HFD-induced amplification of IMQ-induced skin inflammation, maintaining disease severity levels similar to LFD-fed controls (Fig. 2n and Extended Data Fig. 6h). We did not observe an increase in TH22 cells in T cell-specific IL-1R1-deficient mice (Extended Data Fig. 6i). Collectively, these results demonstrate that short-term HFD exacerbates IMQ-induced type 17 inflammation through IL-1R1+ TH17 cells in the skin lesion.

We next examined the mechanistic basis underlying CD4+ T cell induction during IMQ challenge with short-term HFD-feeding. As IL-1α and IL-1β signal through IL-1R135, we investigated whether HFD feeding combined with IMQ challenge increases their expression in the skin. We performed bulk RNA-seq analysis of whole ear tissues from mice that were fed either LFD or HFD and subsequently challenged with IMQ (Supplementary Table 2). Consistent with our earlier findings (Extended Data Fig. 4a,b), the ears of mice fed HFD exhibited a marked upregulation of type 3 cytokine transcripts, including Il17a and Il17f, alongside genes involved in chemotaxis signalling such as Cxcl2, Cxcl3, Ccl3 and Fpr1 (Fig. 3a and Extended Data Fig. 7a). Although both Il1a and Il1b were upregulated in lesional ear skin from HFD-fed mice, the diet-associated increase was more pronounced for Il1b, which increased approximately 3.9-fold (Extended Data Fig. 7b). This pronounced increase in Il1b coincided with a significant upregulation of Nlrp3 (Fig. 3a and Extended Data Fig. 7b). Gene expression analyses of immune cells sorted from the lesions of 15 humans with psoriasis also revealed expression of NLRP3 and IL1B (with specific enrichment in myeloid cells) (Extended Data Fig. 7m–o).

Only peak values were tested in b and n. For d, P values were corrected for multiple comparisons using the Holm–Šídák method. *P < 0.05, **P <0.01, ***P < 0.001.

Assembly of the canonical NLRP3-dependent inflammasome leads to the proteolytic cleavage of pro-caspase-1 into active caspase-1, which subsequently processes pro-IL-1β into its mature, active form2,8. We therefore hypothesized that the NLRP3-dependent inflammasome may be important in driving differentiation of IL-1R1+ TH17 cells in the skin of mice fed HFD during disease development. Consistent with this, genetic ablation of NLRP3 abolished this response: HFD-fed Nlrp3–/– mice did not develop exacerbated disease, in contrast to WT controls (Fig. 3b–d), and Nlrp3 deficiency similarly prevented WD-enhanced inflammation relative to CD (Extended Data Fig. 7c–e). Furthermore, Nlrp3 deficiency prevented the HFD-induced increase in IL-1R1+ TH17 cells and IL-1β protein levels observed in WT mice (Fig. 3e–g). Importantly, Nlrp3 deficiency did not confer metabolic protection after short-term HFD feeding. HFD-fed Nlrp3–/– mice exhibited glucose excursion curves and area under the curve (AUC) values comparable to those of the WT controls (Extended Data Fig. 7f,g), indicating that the attenuation of skin inflammation in Nlrp3–/– mice occurs despite modestly increased glucose intolerance. To independently confirm the role of NLRP3, we topically treated WT mice with MCC950, a selective NLRP3 inhibitor, or vehicle. MCC950 treatment protected against HFD-amplified exacerbation of IMQ-induced inflammation (Extended Data Fig. 7h,i), with marked reductions in lesional TH17 cells and neutrophils (Extended Data Fig. 7j,k). Together, these findings establish NLRP3 as a critical amplifier of inflammation during IMQ challenge under brief HFD feeding.

To identify the cellular source of Nlrp3 and Il1b, we sorted lesional CD45.2+ cells from LFD- or HFD-fed mice after IMQ challenge and performed scRNA-seq (Fig. 3h–j). Clustering revealed diverse myeloid and lymphoid populations, confirmed by cell-type-defining marker expression (Extended Data Fig. 5g). Nlrp3 and Il1b were most strongly expressed in neutrophils (Fig. 3i,j). Quantification showed that neutrophil numbers increased with HFD feeding alone, even without IMQ challenge (Fig. 3k); neutrophils rose further after IMQ challenge (Fig. 3l). Notably, semaglutide did not alter HFD-induced neutrophil accumulation in the skin under the baseline conditions (Extended Data Fig. 3q). Consistent with transcriptional priming of the NLRP3 inflammasome, HFD-fed ear skin before IMQ challenge showed increased expression of Il1b and Nlrp3 (Extended Data Fig. 7l). Thus, short-term HFD establishes a neutrophil-enriched and inflammasome-primed tissue state, whereas IMQ provides the acute inflammatory signal required for productive IL-1β protein accumulation and downstream IL-1R1-dependent TH17 amplification. We next examined how rapidly neutrophil accumulation in skin responds to dietary change. Flow cytometry profiling revealed that neutrophil numbers, but not CD4+ or CD8+ T cells, γδ T cells, B cells or monocytes, showed the largest early increase after short-term HFD feeding and returned to near the baseline 7 days after switching back to the LFD (Fig. 3m). Finally, depletion of neutrophils with anti-Ly6G antibodies abrogated HFD-induced ear thickening during IMQ treatment (Fig. 3n), establishing neutrophils as required mediators of the diet-amplified inflammatory response.

We wondered whether this effect of coincident dietary state extended beyond the skin. To test this, we examined the lung in an experiment in which mice were fed HFD or LFD for 1 week and then challenged intranasally with LPS. We observed a significant increase (around fivefold) in neutrophil counts just after HFD feeding (before LPS treatment) (Extended Data Fig. 8a). After challenge with LPS, HFD-fed mice showed an increased change in lung weight and heightened TH17 inflammation relative to the LFD-fed controls (Extended Data Fig. 8b–d). This response was abolished by neutrophil depletion or T-cell-specific loss of Il1r1 (Extended Data Fig. 8e,f). Thus, coincident dietary state amplifies acute inflammatory responses in a mechanistically similar manner across tissues, indicating that this effect is not skin restricted.

Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by onset, recovery and repeated recurrence36. Inflammatory memory is increasingly recognized as a tissue-retained property that may facilitate relapse at sites of previous inflammation11,37,38. To test whether diet over disease onset (DODO) shapes disease trajectory beyond the initial flare, we developed an IMQ-induced inflammation recurrence model (Fig. 4a). Mice were placed on LFD or HFD for 1 week, then subjected to daily IMQ challenge for 6 days while continuing the assigned diet. As expected, the HFD-fed mice exhibited roughly twofold greater ear thickening compared with the LFD-fed control mice during the acute phase. Thereafter, all mice were returned to LFD and IMQ treatment was discontinued. After approximately 25 days of recovery, both groups appeared fully resolved by gross examination, ear thickness measurement, histology, bulk RNA-seq and serum cytokine profiling (Fig. 4b,c and Extended Data Fig. 9a–d).
